$comment: P63 [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNMENT-CEILING-REFUSES-WHAT-TWO-REFERENCES-RUN]]: the runtime witness that a PAGE-ALIGNED request is honored end to end. Before this cycle every construct in main.c was `error[S_AlignasExceedsMax]` -- the requestable ceiling was a hardcoded 256 in the semantic ladder, hand-copied into `Alignment::fromBytes` and again into the interner's `representableCompositeAlign`, three owners of one fact. It is now DECLARED, per target, as `aggregateLayout.maxRequestedAlignment` (268435456 on both shipped targets). $$ THE REFERENCE TABLE, each probed SEPARATELY, BUILD **and** RUN with the exit code asserted, subject `struct __attribute__((aligned(N))) big { char c; };` and its `_Alignas(N)` twin, CONTROL arm N=16 green throughout: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both RUN 42 at N = 512, 1024, 4096, 8192, 16384, 65536, 2^20 and 2^28; gcc refuses 2^29 BY NAME ("requested alignment '536870912' exceeds maximum 268435456") and clang at 2^29 BUILDS and then answers with an `_Alignof` that disagrees with the request, so it casts no vote there under "the union is over what WORKS, not what is ACCEPTED". aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 give gcc's SAME 2^28, which is why the key is a TARGET fact. $ WHY IT RUNS RATHER THAN COMPILES: the OLD failure was a loud refusal (nothing was ever miscompiled, which is exactly why every gate stayed green over it), and the NEW failure mode is the opposite -- an alignment accepted and then not applied is SILENT. So the exit code is derived from the ADDRESSES the linker chose and from the real field offsets, never from a constant: 4096 appears only as the request. $ THE SINK IS ASSERTED, not the absence of an error: each decorated member follows a `char`, so its offset AND the aggregate size both move when the request lands (0/4096/8192 vs the parse-and-drop 0/1/2). $ NOT EXERCISED HERE, deliberately: the SECOND and narrower per-FORMAT ceiling on a statically allocated object (what the image can PLACE it at). On PE that is the document's declared `SectionAlignment`, 4096, so this example sits AT that boundary on every shipped format and above none -- a request above it is refused by name with `K_StaticObjectOveralignedForFormat`, pinned by its own unit test.
